negative_findings.description: No Ukrainian PSP in this cell was found to publish a structured, dedicated merchant case-study library in the Western SaaS sense.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fondy's partners page (fetched directly) carries a single named testimonial (Cloud9 Fulfilment) and no case-study directory; WayForPay, LiqPay, Portmone, iPay and Platon searches surfaced product, tariff and integration pages but no case-study index. Merchant-level evidence has to be reconstructed from integrator blogs, press interviews and marketplace connector lists.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Case-study collection for UA payments must be an inference pipeline over indirect sources, not a scrape of vendor case-study pages; budget for entity extraction from trade press and agency sites.

negative_findings.description: Canonical URLs for several actors were not confirmed by direct fetch in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: liqpay.ua, wayforpay.com, ipay.ua, platon.ua, easypay.ua, plata.mono, concordfintech.solutions and mustpay.tech were identified through search result metadata and third-party articles rather than by successful fetch; only fondy.io/gb/partners/ was fetched directly. The exact NBU payment-infrastructure register URL on bank.gov.ua was not pinned down.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Downstream liveness verification must resolve these, especially plata.mono (branding vs. domain) and the NBU register deep link, before they are treated as stable collection targets.

negative_findings.result_summary: Concord Bank itself appears in Ukrainian Wikipedia/Minfin as a wound-down bank, while Concord Fintech Solutions and MustPay present as live ecosystem/vendor brands. Which legal entity currently holds processing/acquiring capability was not resolved from open search.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Treating 'Concord' as one live processor would misstate the competitive set; the register lookup is required to disambiguate before any market conclusion.

negative_findings.description: No established Ukrainian-language term was found for a PSP 'partner directory' as a distinct published artefact.
negative_findings.result_summary: Queries using 'партнерська програма', 'партнери', 'каталог інтеграцій' returned CMS/module lists and knowledge-base articles rather than partner directories; the artefact type appears not to exist locally under any consistent name.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Search strategies ported from Western markets will under-retrieve; local retrieval should target 'інтеграції', 'модулі для CMS' and help-centre subdomains instead.

coverage_gaps.description: E-wallet and P2P/remittance providers in Ukraine (as distinct from card-acquiring PSPs) were only lightly covered; no dedicated wallet-provider partner directory was located.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated pass on 'електронний гаманець Україна', 'емітент електронних грошей', wallet brands and NBU's e-money issuer list; include mobile-operator and marketplace wallets.

coverage_gaps.description: Merchant-win and bank-acquiring partnership announcements were found as isolated examples (WayForPay-LiqPay-Raiffeisen, iPay-Vchasno.Kasa) rather than as a systematically collectable stream.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Stand up keyword monitoring across psm7.com, fintechinsider.com.ua, speka.ua, kosht.media and biz.nv.ua on PSP brand names plus 'партнерство/еквайринг/інтеграція', and back it with the NBU register diff for entity-level ground truth.

coverage_gaps.description: The NBU Payment Infrastructure Register was identified conceptually but not located as a concrete, downloadable endpoint.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Locate and pin the register's page/dataset on bank.gov.ua (and any open-data mirror) and make it the spine that every PSP candidate is joined to.

coverage_gaps.description: English-language sources for this cell are dominated by low-credibility aggregators (ensun, sourceforge, comparison blogs); the substantive material is almost entirely Ukrainian.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Weight Ukrainian-language collection heavily for this cell and use English sources only for internationalising players such as Fondy and Tranzzo.

brief: Ukraine's payments-native competitive layer is publicly legible but unevenly documented: the major gateways (LiqPay, WayForPay, Fondy, Portmone, iPay, Platon, Tranzzo) plus newer ecosystem entrants (RozetkaPay, NovaPay, plata by mono, EasyPay) all maintain product, tariff and developer-documentation pages, and Fondy is the only one with an explicit tiered channel-partner program. Formal merchant case-study libraries are largely absent, so merchant-level evidence must be reconstructed indirectly from integrator and CRM/agency integration pages, iPaaS connector catalogues, and Ukrainian fintech trade press (psm7.com, fintechinsider.com.ua), which is also the fastest channel for acquiring-partnership announcements. The Concord cluster (Concord Fintech Solutions, MustPay, ProCard-style processing) is the least transparent part of the cell and needs entity-level disambiguation. The NBU payment infrastructure register and the September 2025 acquiring rule change should anchor the whole cell: the register enumerates legitimate PSPs and the rule change is already reshaping PSP-bank-merchant contractual structures.
